sections.readable_text: The standard Gaussian elimination for a [MATH: 3 \times 3] system can be described as follows:

sections.normalized_html:
1. If [MATH: a_{11} eq 0] and [MATH: a_{11} eq 1,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_1:=R_1/a_{11}.]

  2. We use first row and the necessary row operations to make the remaining entries of the first column below [MATH: a_{11}] equal to [MATH: 0.] Namely,

    • if [MATH: a_{21} eq 0,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_2:=R_2 + (-a_{21})R_1;]

    • if [MATH: a_{31} eq 0,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_3:=R_3 + (-a_{31})R_1.]

  3. If [MATH: a_{22} eq 1,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_2:=R_2/a_{22}.]

  4. We use the second row and the necessary row operation to make the entry below [MATH: a_{22}] equal to [MATH: 0.] Namely,

    • if [MATH: a_{32} eq 0,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_3:=R_3 + (-a_{32})R_2.]

1. If [MATH: a_{11} \neq 0] and [MATH: a_{11} \neq 1,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_1:=R_1/a_{11}.]
2. We use first row and the necessary row operations to make the remaining entries of the first column below [MATH: a_{11}] equal to [MATH: 0.] Namely,

- if [MATH: a_{21} \neq 0,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_2:=R_2 + (-a_{21})R_1;]
- if [MATH: a_{31} \neq 0,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_3:=R_3 + (-a_{31})R_1.]
3. If [MATH: a_{22} \neq 1,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_2:=R_2/a_{22}.]
4. We use the second row and the necessary row operation to make the entry below [MATH: a_{22}] equal to [MATH: 0.] Namely,

- if [MATH: a_{32} \neq 0,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_3:=R_3 + (-a_{32})R_2.]

1. If [MATH: a_{33} \neq 1,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_3:=R_3/a_{33}.]

  2. In some exceptional cases, such as when the element on the diagonal is equal to [MATH: 0,] we first need to exchange rows. Then proceed using the same steps as above.

Content:
The standard Gaussian elimination for a [MATH: 3 \times 3] system can be described as follows:

Content:
1. If [MATH: a_{11} \neq 0] and [MATH: a_{11} \neq 1,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_1:=R_1/a_{11}.]
2. We use first row and the necessary row operations to make the remaining entries of the first column below [MATH: a_{11}] equal to [MATH: 0.] Namely,

- if [MATH: a_{21} \neq 0,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_2:=R_2 + (-a_{21})R_1;]
- if [MATH: a_{31} \neq 0,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_3:=R_3 + (-a_{31})R_1.]
3. If [MATH: a_{22} \neq 1,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_2:=R_2/a_{22}.]
4. We use the second row and the necessary row operation to make the entry below [MATH: a_{22}] equal to [MATH: 0.] Namely,

- if [MATH: a_{32} \neq 0,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_3:=R_3 + (-a_{32})R_2.]

Content:
1. If [MATH: a_{33} \neq 1,] then we use the row operation [MATH: R_3:=R_3/a_{33}.]
2. In some exceptional cases, such as when the element on the diagonal is equal to [MATH: 0,] we first need to exchange rows. Then proceed using the same steps as above.

Content:
Carrying out the above algorithm will convert the matrix to row echelon form.
